chunks: We were told by Hasan ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn al-Muaddab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Bakr ibn Abdullah, from Nasr ibn Ubaid [Allah], from Nasr ibn Muzahim, that he said: I was told by Abdul-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, from al-A'mash, from Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, that he said:

Abu Sufyan approached, while Mu'awiya was following him, and the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family, said: 'O Allah, curse the follower and the followed. O Allah, it is upon You to ruin the Aqi'is.' Ibn al-Bara' said to his father: Who is the Aqi'is? He said: Mu'awiya.

key_terms.أَبُو سُفْيَان: Abu Sufyan, a prominent companion and father of Mu'awiya
key_terms.التَّابِعَ وَالْمَتْبُوعَ: The follower and the followed, referring to Mu'awiya following his father Abu Sufyan
key_terms.الْأَقِيعِس: A specific term used in the hadith to describe Mu'awiya, often translated as 'the belittled lordotic' or 'the arrogant'
key_terms.مُعَاوِيَةُ: Mu'awiya, son of Abu Sufyan and founder of the Umayyad Caliphate

ai.seo_question: Who is referred to as 'al-Aqi'is' in the hadith of Abu Sufyan and Mu'awiya?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family) invokes divine curse upon Abu Sufyan and his son Mu'awiya, specifically identifying Mu'awiya as 'al-Aqi'is' (the one who follows or the follower). This term underscores Mu'awiya's political and spiritual subservience to his father, a key dynamic in early Shia historiography regarding the Umayyad rise to power. The supplication highlights the Prophet's foresight regarding the Umayyad dynasty's influence, a theme central to Shia eschatological and historical narratives.
